title: Legacy AC2 and BR1 load DELEGATION_LIMIT through the reference-data service, but the Ownership Map keeps delegation_limit with P4 rwb-access
source: Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables (delegation_limit owner P4, asm ASM-A6-tables-4; reference_version, reference_row and lov_value owner P3); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 043 Reference data service with versioned tables v2.md sections 7 AC2, 8 BR1 and 10; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 line 302
section: 3 Preconditions; 8 Business rules BR1; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.7 Tables owned
description: The preserved legacy story treats DELEGATION_LIMIT as one of the twelve reference tables that the reference-data service loads, versions and serves: AC2 loads it with 24 rows and BR1 lists it with the other eleven codes. The Ownership Map rules that the DoA table is P4 rwb-access (Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 v3 T3.1; ASM-A6-tables-4) while reference data stays with P3 (DP-07; ASM-A6-tables-5). Both readings cannot hold for one table: either the DoA table is duplicated in both services or the reference surface serves eleven of the twelve codes. The legacy AC text stays verbatim because the story is preserved, so the conflict is carried by this row and by the target reading in sections 3, 8 and 11 of RWB-P3-E1043-APP and in sections 2, 3, 8, 12.2 and 12.7 of RWB-P3-E1043-CON.
evidence: RWB-E1-043 section 7 AC2 (loads table DELEGATION_LIMIT with 24 rows), section 8 BR1 (twelve codes including DELEGATION_LIMIT), section 10 (approval of DELEGATION_LIMIT follows doa.txt rule 11); Ownership Map tables row delegation_limit with asm ASM-A6-tables-4 and ruling kept with P4; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (P4 REST GET /doa-limits) and slide 41 (P4 DoA table); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 line 302 (delegation limits held as versioned reference data)
proposed: Keep the legacy AC2 wording in the preserved story and apply the target reading: the reference surface of rwb-case serves the eleven non-DoA codes, a delegation limit is read from the rwb-access DoA operation GET /doa-limits declared in RWB-P3-E1043-CON section 12.2, and no copy of delegation_limit is created in rwb_case.

title: The column definitions of each reference table code and the element types of the reference resources have no source field by field
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 043 Reference data service with versioned tables v2.md sections 11, 12 and 13; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T3.2 reference_version and reference_row; FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.23.3.2; RWB-P3-E1019-CON section 11
section: 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: (a) The legacy plan assumes that the column definitions per reference table code exist as data, but no source lists the columns, their types, their required flags or their key columns for any of the twelve codes. (b) The element types, lengths and required flags of the load, check-result and version-list resources that RWB-P3-E1043-CON publishes are not specified. (c) RWB-P3-E1019-CON already records that the remaining lov_value columns have no source, so the same gap runs through two stories of this service.
evidence: RWB-E1-043 section 13 build step 2 (build the column definitions per reference table code) and section 11 (field ids for reference_version, reference_row and the two lov_value fields only); TSD P3 v3 T3.2 lists the two tables field by field but no per-code column set; FSD P3 v4 A2.23 field catalog shows recovery_case columns and none of a reference table; RWB-P3-E1019-CON section 11 field identifiers with no source
proposed: Hold the per-code column definitions as data beside LOV-REF-TABLE and let the load row check read them; the contract publishes the resource element names of this key and leaves the types to the review with the data steward; the placeholder stays in sections 11 and 13 until the definitions are agreed.

title: The answer of a dated read with no version in force, and the rights of the verify and the rollback, are not stated
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 043 Reference data service with versioned tables v2.md sections 7 AC9, 10, 12 and 14; Ownership Map v1 sheet API (POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/verify and /rollback, asm ASM-A6-api-4)
section: 12.1 REST operations provided; 14 Validation and messages
description: (a) The legacy contract fixes 404 for an unknown load with MSG-P4-003, 409 for a duplicate valid from and 422 for a failed check, but it does not fix the answer of a read whose date has no approved version in force: AC9 fixes only the engine behaviour and the alert, and the as-built read is an in-process call with no HTTP answer. (b) The Ownership Map names the verify and the rollback operation of the reference load but no source gives the right each needs, while the legacy story gives C to the load and A to the approve.
evidence: RWB-E1-043 section 12 error rows (401 MSG-P4-001, 403 MSG-P4-002, 404 MSG-P4-003, 409 MSG-P3-027, 422 MSG-P3-027 or MSG-GEN-001); RWB-E1-043 section 7 AC9 and section 10 (Reference data C, A and R, RW-RISK approves); Ownership Map API rows for GET /admin/lists/{listCode}, POST /admin/reference-loads, .../verify, .../approve and .../rollback with no right column in any source
proposed: The dated read answers 404 with MSG-P3-027 naming the table code and the date and never an older version, a default row or an empty list; the verify and the rollback require Reference data A, the right the legacy story gives the approval, with the separation of duty of section 10 unchanged.

title: The rule package registry and the workbook object are declared in the P3 module and owned by P7
source: Legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 3, 4, 11, 12 and 13 (rule_package_version writes, the Blob workbook, RulePackageEffectiveDateJob); TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T2.1 (RulePackageRepository) and T3.1 (rule_package and rule_package_version 'owned by P4'); Ownership Map v1 (rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case, owner P7, ruling ASM-A6-tables-3); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 27 and 41; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15
section: s2 Business rationale; s9 State transitions; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s19 Out of scope
description: The legacy story loads, approves, promotes and rolls back a package version and writes rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case, the generated DRL and the workbook Blob object from inside the case module, and its preconditions require a job_catalog row for RulePackageEffectiveDateJob. The ownership ruling and Architecture v5 put the four registry tables, the model registry, the workbook object, the five authoring operations and the 00:01 promotion in rwb-decision, which leaves rwb-case with the evaluated copy, the case fact mapping, the version pin, the scenario gate and a consumed contract only. Three of the fifteen legacy criteria therefore name an artefact this service does not own: the rule_package_version.checksum and Blob metadata of AC15, the rule_package_version row and Blob object of AC13, and the promotion wording behind AC1 and AC4. This story proves those against the rwb-decision contract mock and carries the registry work to RWB-P7-E1073-APP, with the real cross-service proof in RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-073 section 13: 'The load writes rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case in one transaction'; section 11: DF-REF-279 to DF-REF-294 are written by this story; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 headings 'rule_package (NEW, owned by P4)', 'rule_package_version (NEW, owned by P4)', 'rule_test_case (NEW, owned by P4)'; Ownership Map v1 owner P7 with ruling ASM-A6-tables-3 'services hold only a local evaluated copy (DP-04)'; Architecture v5 slide 41 P7 'approvals, central decision ledger, DMN model registry'; Temporal and Drools slide 15 'governance ... is central in rwb-decision (P7)'
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-073 (AC1, AC4, AC13, AC15; sections 3, 4, 11, 12 and 13)
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the P3 tech lead
proposed: Keep the registry, the workbook object, the five authoring operations, the approval, the promotion Schedule JOB-20 and the rollback in RWB-P7-E1073-APP under ASM-A6-tables-3; keep the case fact mapping, the version pin, the scenario gate and the consumed contract in RWB-P3-E1073-APP and RWB-P3-E1073-CON; correct the TSD P3 v3 ownership labels for the four tables; prove the registry statements against the rwb-decision contract mock here and against the real service in RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG.

title: The five authoring operations and the two rule reads have no Ownership Map row and no field-level shape
source: Ownership Map v1 api section (P3 and P7 rows); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (P7 IN: POST /rule-models, GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}); legacy RWB-E1-073 section 12 (the five admin paths on the monolith base); TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T2.2 (RuleResult, RuleCatalog.row)
section: s11 Data; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13 Build steps
description: RWB-P3-E1073-CON and RWB-P3-E1073-APP consume seven operations of rwb-decision: the load, the version list, the approve, the rollback, the dry run, the model read and the catalog read. The Ownership Map lists no row for any of them, Architecture v5 slide 14 names only POST /rule-models and GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} and the legacy section 12 gives the five admin paths on the retired monolith base with no owner in the target. The rollback and dry-run answer shapes, the catalog element names and the property types of both reads are therefore assumed here. This key fixes the element names, the rights, the answers, the error codes and the fakes on Day 1 and leaves the types to the review with the rwb-decision owner.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 api rows for P7 list GET /cases/{caseId}/recommendation, GET /approvals, the three approval actions, GET /decision-log and GET /decision-log/{entryId} and no rule-package or rule-model row; Architecture v5 slide 14 P7 IN: 'REST GET /decisions?caseId= ... POST /rule-models, GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}'; legacy RWB-E1-073 section 12 paths under the monolith base; TSD P3 v3 T2.2 gives the Java signatures RuleResult and RuleRow but no wire shape
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the solution architect
proposed: Add the seven operations to the P7 rows of the Ownership Map and to the rwb-decision API file with their rights, answers and error codes, and publish the model and catalog resources with packageCode, versionLabel, checksum, valid-from date, compiler version, ruleId, action_text, owner_role, timer_spec, target_queue_code and outputs; until then the RWB-P3-E1073-CON baseline and its WireMock fakes carry the assumed shapes and paths.

title: The KieBase cache sizing, the JVM heap and the storage of a local model artefact are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-073 preconditions ('rules.testcases.min = 50 (assumed)' and 'drools.kiebase.cache.max = 20') and section 13; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 27 (evaluation under 300 ms, cache, checksum); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 16 (KieBaseRegistry, LRU, max 20)
section: s11 Data; s13 Solution plan; s17 Guardrails; s19 Out of scope (RWB-P3-E1073-INF)
description: No source states the heap a pod of rwb-case needs to hold the KieBase cache of at most 20 package versions plus the working set of the service, and no source says whether a compiled model may be written to a local volume or is rebuilt in memory after a restart. The legacy story names the cache bound and the test count as parameters, marks the test count assumed and gives no deployment figure at all. RWB-P3-E1073-INF exposes the heap, the cache bound and the model life cycle as reviewed values per environment, proves them with a load test that holds the cache bound and evaluates under load, and records them as assumptions rather than as business values.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-073 precondition: 'rules.testcases.min = 50 (assumed) and drools.kiebase.cache.max = 20 are in the catalog'; Architecture v5 slide 27: 'Load GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}, verify checksum, swap in' and 'Evaluate Inside an activity, under 300 ms'; Temporal and Drools slide 16: 'KieBaseRegistry holds one KieBase per package version (LRU, max 20), never recompiled per call', with no memory figure and no storage statement
owner_role: SCB IT infrastructure with the rwb-case owner team
proposed: Size the pod by a load test that holds the cache bound of 20 package versions and evaluates under load, record the heap request, the heap limit and the cache bound per environment as reviewed values, keep the evaluated copy in memory only, and confirm the values with the platform owner before the wave 1 release.

title: No source gives the readiness gate, the probe timings, the ports, the certificate subject or the image-scan window
source: Legacy RWB-E1-073 preconditions (the rwb-decision dependency and the module identity); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 20 and 27 (mTLS, one namespace, the model in force); TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T2.5 (temporal.target, mTLS certificates from the ACE internal CA, the worker identity)
section: s11 Data; s13 Solution plan; s14 Validation and messages; s19 Out of scope (RWB-P3-E1073-INF)
description: The deployment story must decide when a pod is ready, with which probe timings, on which ports, with which certificate subject and with which image-scan window and patch cadence. No source gives any of them: the legacy story names no deployment value, Architecture v5 gives the mechanism of mTLS and the model in force but no threshold, and TSD P3 v3 gives the parameter names without values. RWB-P3-E1073-INF therefore exposes every one of them as a reviewed value per environment under one assumption, so the operator sees a pod without a model in force before a case reaches it without the story inventing a business value.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-073 precondition: 'the rwb-decision front end presents a certificate the platform certificate authority issued' equivalent wording and no port or timing; Architecture v5 slide 11 and slide 20 give mTLS and the namespace shape only; TSD P3 v3 T2.5: 'temporal.target | Frontend gRPC address per environment | Internal only; port 7233' with no probe, readiness, scan or certificate-subject value; no threshold appears in FSD P3 v4 or the Drools design
owner_role: SCB IT infrastructure with the platform administrator
proposed: Record the readiness gate, the probe timings, the ports, the certificate subject and the image-scan window as reviewed values per environment in the deployment files, confirm them with the platform and security owners at SIT, and keep every one of them out of code and out of a chart constant.

title: The treatment entity moves to S2 while the legacy story holds it in P3, and the case side consumes TreatmentApproved which the event catalogue does not list for rwb-case
source: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (tables treatment, timer, dp_treatment); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18, 41, 42, 44; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 9 and 14; legacy story RWB-E2-004 sections 1, 3, 4 and 13
section: s1 Story; s2 Business rationale; s4 Flow; s11 Data; s12.4 Events consumed; s19 Out of scope
description: RWB-E2-004 built the treatment row, its repository, its service and its published interface inside P3 Case and workflow, with JOB-05 and the TimerScheduler port firing the plan timers. The target splits the capability three ways: Architecture v5 slide 41 and slide 18 give S2 rwb-treatment the treatments, the settlement and deed-in-lieu agreements and the plan timers in schema rwb_treatment; the Ownership Map gives `timer` to P3 with the ruling that the row is only the screen projection while the clock is a durable Temporal timer in CaseWorkflow and TimerDue and JOB-05 are retired; and the Temporal and Drools design puts the restructure stage and the cure-period wait in TreatmentWorkflow on rwb-treatment. The case side must therefore consume TreatmentApproved and PaymentMissed, yet Architecture v5 slide 42 lists only rwb-comms and rwb-payment as consumers of TreatmentApproved, and no source states which of the two services writes the plan timer, which one sets PLAN_RUNNING and PLAN_CURE_PERIOD, or which one publishes CaseStateChanged for the plan move. The legacy story's AC1 to AC14 name the treatment write, the timer write and the route move as one service's work, so every criterion of the split needs one stated seam.
evidence: ownership.json tables.treatment.owner = S2, basis 'Architecture v5 slide 41 (S2 owns treatments, contracts, settlement and deed-in-lieu agreements, plan timers) and slide 18 S2 DB line; TSD S2 v2 T3.1'; tables.timer.ruling 'timer stays with P3 as the screen projection behind GET /cases/{caseId}/timers, while the clock itself is a durable Temporal timer in CaseWorkflow; TimerDue and JOB-05 are retired', asm ASM-A6-tables-12; Architecture v5 slide 42 row '10 | TreatmentApproved | rwb-treatment | rwb.treatment.events.v1 | rwb-comms, rwb-payment'; slide 44 'JOB-05 Timer check every 5 min all durable timers (retired)'; Temporal and Drools design slide 14 note 'rwb-case forwards the event to the running stage child, TreatmentWorkflow on queue rwb-treatment'; RWB-E2-004 section 13 'Package. S2 package recovery.treatment.record for the treatment record; P3 package recovery.casewf.plan for the plan timer listener'.
legacy_ref: RWB-E2-004 (AC1, AC2, AC4 to AC9, AC11 to AC14; legacy sections 3, 4, 11, 13)
proposed: Confirm in the wave 2 architecture review that the treatment, its terms and its approval are S2's and never written in rwb_case, that rwb-case consumes rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1 and rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1 and holds the case route state, the timer projection and the durable plan timer in CaseWorkflow, and add rwb-case to the consumer list of TreatmentApproved in the event catalogue so the subscription is contractual.

title: The 01:30 treatment extract has no owner in the target and its DP04 read path and freshness element are not in the Ownership Map
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 37, 41 and 44; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (tables dp_treatment, lake_copy_watermark, data_product); legacy story RWB-E2-004 sections 4, 5 and 12
section: s4 Flow; s5 Exception paths X7; s11 Data; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s19 Out of scope
description: The legacy story owns the extract step: JOB-15 Reporting extract at 01:30 reads changed treatments through TreatmentRecords.changedSince, writes the DP04 treatment data product, and shows the previous business date with MSG-P1-001 when it fails. In the target the data lake is removed (DP-17; ADR-018) and the job map gives JOB-15 to rwb-reporting at 01:30 with an Airflow trigger and no data lake, while the Ownership Map gives dp_treatment to P1 rwb-source-data as a dated copy built from events. No source says who owns the treatment extract step, which service serves the DP04 treatment rows, or what path and what freshness element the case side reads for AC3 and AC10; the Ownership Map API section carries no data-product operation at all, and the lake_copy_watermark ruling records that the only legacy table tied to the removed lake is dropped rather than replaced.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 'JOB-15 | Reporting extract | 01:30 | rwb-reporting | Airflow trigger (no data lake)'; slide 37 and DP-17 'no data lake connection'; ownership.json tables.dp_treatment.owner = P1 with ruling 'The live treatment and guarantee records stay with S2 and S3; the dated DP04 copies stay with P1 as the data engine (TSD P1 v3), built from events and read-only for reporting', asm ASM-A6-tables-14; tables.lake_copy_watermark.ruling 'lake_copy_watermark is a P1 legacy table with no target: the data lake is removed'; RWB-E2-004 section 4 step 10 'JOB-15 Reporting extract: each night reads changed treatments through TreatmentRecords.changedSince(...) and writes the treatment data product (DP04)'; section 12 'JOB-15 Reporting extract (nightly 01:30)' as a P3 job; the api section of ownership.json has no data-product row.
proposed: Record the owner of the treatment extract as P9 rwb-reporting on JOB-15 with the DP04 copy in rwb_source_data, publish the case-facing read GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP04/records with its freshness element in the Ownership Map and the P1 API file, and state in the event catalogue that the copy is built from the treatment events.

title: No source fixes the plan-timer fields, types or required flags of the timers answer behind GET /cases/{caseId}/timers
source: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api 'GET /cases/{caseId}/timers', tables timer); Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5 TSD P3 v3 T3.1 and T3.2; legacy story RWB-E2-004 sections 11 and 12
section: s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s13 Solution plan (Database)
description: The ruling keeps the `timer` row as the projection behind the timers operation and the plan timers carry `treatment_id` (DF-WRK-042), with the timer types INSTALLMENT_DUE and CURE_PERIOD already present in LOV-TIMER. What no source gives is the answer shape: whether the timers resource returns `treatmentId`, whether a plan timer carries the rule ID and the package version it was created under, whether `expiresAt` is a zone-qualified instant or a local date-time, and which of these properties are required. TSD P3 v3 names the table columns but not the REST properties, the Ownership Map names the operation but not its schema, and the legacy story's own contract section described the table and the TimerScheduler port rather than the JSON shape. The app, contract and test stories of this key and the wave 2 harness all read the same answer, so the shape has to be fixed once.
evidence: ownership.json tables.timer.ruling 'timer stays with P3 as the screen projection behind GET /cases/{caseId}/timers'; api 'GET /cases/{caseId}/timers' owner P3 with no response shape; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 columns DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036, DF-WRK-042 to DF-WRK-044 and T3.2 'LOV-TIMER | SERVICE_LEVEL, NOTICE_PERIOD, CURE_PERIOD, PRESCRIPTION, HEARING_DEADLINE, OFFER_VALIDITY, HOLDING_AGE, CLAIM_DEADLINE, INSTALLMENT_DUE'; RWB-E2-004 section 12 'GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers (P3) returns Timer[]' with no field list.
legacy_ref: RWB-E2-004 (AC2, AC12, AC14; legacy section 11 and 12)
proposed: Fix the plan-timer properties in the RWB-P3-E2004-CON baseline review with the timer owner (RWB-P3-E1028-CON) and the harness: treatmentId, timerType, startedAt, expiresAt, warnAt, paused and status, all optional within major version 1, with expiresAt as an offset date-time, and record them in the rwb-case OpenAPI file.

title: No source gives the alert values for the plan-timer projection, the subscription lag, the DP04 freshness or the exception-queue count
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 28 and 44; legacy story RWB-E2-004 sections 5 and 13; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s17
section: s11 Data; s13 Solution plan (Alert mapping); s14 Validation and messages
description: The deployment alerts on the projection lag between arming a plan timer and reading its row, on the lag of the two subscriptions, on the `.dlt` count, on the exception-queue count of refused plan steps and on the freshness of the DP04 treatment product, but no source gives a threshold, a window or a band. The legacy story names only a five-minute timer check that the target retires and a consumer retry limit of 3; the FSD and TSD P3 give no operational value, and the architecture extract names the alert as a capability without a number. Every value therefore has to be a values-file entry with a provisional default, and the runbook entry each alert links has to state that the value is provisional.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 'JOB-21 Stuck workflow scan | every 5 min | platform | visibility query + alert' with no threshold; slide 28 'stops at once (no retry); stuck-case alert' with no value; RWB-E2-004 section 5 X6 'retries the event 3 times' and section 13 'Event consumer retry limit 3 (NFR-026)' as the only numeric operational value; no threshold appears in FSD P3 v4, TSD P3 v3 or the Ownership Map.
proposed: Set the values in the rwb-case values files as provisional defaults, confirm them at UAT with the service owner and the platform observability owner, and record the agreed values in the runbook entry each alert links.

title: The cap a per-owner queue count is measured against: the queue capacity or the member's personal capacity
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-011 v1, section 8 BR6 and section 12 GET /queues; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3, T3.1 queue.capacity_cap (DF-WRK-007) and queue_member.capacity (DF-WRK-048); FSD P3 Case and workflow v4, A2.6 AC-ALT-P3-006-02
section: 8. Business rules BR6; 11. Data; 12.1 REST operations provided (GET /queues)
description: The legacy story measures every owner of a queue against one queue-level cap, while the target model gives the queue a capacity_cap and the member a personal capacity, and the FSD works an example in which one member of a queue holds a capacity of 40. No source says which of the two feeds atCap on the queue answer, or which one wins when both are set.
evidence: BR6: "An owner at or above the queue's caseload cap is shown at cap", source "Queue field capacity_cap; DL23"; AC2: "each owner in MTG-BKK-CO shows their open case count against the cap of 150"; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 queue_member DF-WRK-048 capacity, integer, optional; FSD P3 v4 AC-ALT-P3-006-02: "member U-11 of queue TDR-BKK-CO has capacity 40 and holds 40 open cases"
owner_role: Product owner for queue and caseload rules
proposed: Fix the cap in force per queue as a rule of the queue reference data: read queue.capacity_cap when the queue sets one, otherwise queue_member.capacity; until that rule is settled the app story reads queue.capacity_cap, which is the cap AC2 fixes at 150.

title: The queue summary fields, their types, and whether the summary is read live or from the queue_measure snapshot
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-011 v1, section 12 GET /queues; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3, T3.1 queue_measure (DF-RPT-020 to DF-RPT-030); FSD P3 Case and workflow v4, A2.18 FEAT-CWC-18 and A2.39 FEAT-WKM-02
section: 11. Data; 12.1 REST operations provided (GET /queues); 13. Solution plan
description: The legacy answer names openCaseCount, oldestEntryDate, oldestAgeDays, breachCount and owners[] with ownerUserId, openCaseCount and atCap, and types none of them. The target table that holds queue measures names different things (depth, unassigned, avg_age_days, max_age_days, owner_min, owner_max, breached, status) and is a reconciled snapshot published on a schedule, while the legacy screen is a live read that must equal the case list count at the moment it is read (AC11). No source says whether the team queue answer is computed from the case rows or read from the snapshot, nor the physical type and length of each field.
evidence: Legacy section 12: "200 Queue[] with the new computed fields openCaseCount, oldestEntryDate, oldestAgeDays, breachCount, owners[] (ownerUserId, openCaseCount, atCap)"; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 queue_measure: DF-RPT-023 depth, DF-RPT-025 avg_age_days, DF-RPT-026 max_age_days, DF-RPT-029 breached, DF-RPT-030 status; FSD P3 v4 A2.18: "publishes them to the case list and Power BI"
proposed: Type the answer as openCaseCount and breachCount integers, oldestAgeDays integer, oldestEntryDate a date and owners[] with an integer openCaseCount and a boolean atCap; compute the five fields live from recovery_case and the open timer of each case, and read queue_measure only as a reconciliation check until the queue-measure story settles which one is in force.

title: The freshness answer, the X-Data-As-Of header and the value of the product placeholder in the stale banner
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-011 v1, section 12 GET /cases and section 14 MSG-P1-001; Ownership Map v1 api row GET /data-products/freshness (P1); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 15, rwb-source-data contract "GET /freshness (business date)"
section: 4. Flow, step 4; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 14. Validation and messages
description: The legacy story carries the business date of the case data in an X-Data-As-Of response header of the list and names a product in MSG-P1-001. In the target the freshness fact belongs to rwb-source-data, whose path is /data-products/freshness in the Ownership Map and /freshness on the architecture slides, and no source says whether rwb-case sets the header from that answer or the composite route composes the banner, nor what the {product} placeholder names on a case list.
evidence: Legacy section 12: "header X-Data-As-Of with the business date of the case data"; MSG-P1-001: "{product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived."; Ownership Map v1: "GET /data-products/freshness" owned by P1; Architecture v5 slide 14: "REST GET /freshness (business date)"
proposed: rwb-case reads the business date from GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness, caches it for the request and the business date, sets X-Data-As-Of on the two case answers and omits the header when the answer does not arrive inside the budget; the composite route renders the banner and fills {product} with the data product name the screen shows.

title: The partial-success shape of a selection and its summary message are not typed
source: Legacy story RWB E2 012 v2 sections 4, 13 and 16 (BulkTransferRunner, MSG-P3-035); FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.40.4.3 AC-EXC-P3-040-04; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 API-P3-006
section: 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria (AC3, AC11); 12 Contract (12.1); 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy screen sends one request per selected case and renders one row per case plus a summary, and the legacy AC11 fixes the outcome as 8 of 10 moved with the two held cases showing MSG-P3-005 and the summary showing MSG-P3-035. No source types the element a row is rendered from, its order, its required fields, or how the summary counts are carried: the transfer operation is declared per case and has no set-level request or response, and the summary is a message text with two placeholders and no schema.
evidence: Legacy section 4 step 8 'for a bulk move, one result per case and the summary'; section 13 'BulkTransferRunner | Sends one request per selected case in sequence and collects the results'; FSD AC-EXC-P3-040-04 'eight cases move And the two held cases show MSG-P3-005 And the summary shows MSG-P3-035 with 8 of 10'; TSD API-P3-006 Request TransferRequest Response Assignment, with no set-level operation anywhere in the P3 API inventory; MSG-P3-035 '{done} of {total} cases were moved. The others show the reason on their row.' has no field table.
owner_role: Solution architect, P3; tech lead of rwb-case
proposed: Fix one selection element in the rwb-case contract: an ordered array with caseId, the assignment or the messageId of the refusal, and the done and total counts; state that the order is the caller's order and that the summary is derived from the array and never from a second call.

title: The at-cap and legal-hold pre-check answers have no typed shape
source: Legacy story RWB E2 012 v2 sections 4, 12 and 14; FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.40.3.1 and A2.41.3.1; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 API-P3-006, T3.1
section: 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths (X3, X4, X6); 7 Acceptance criteria (AC5, AC7, AC12); 12 Contract (12.1)
description: A move must be refused before any write when the target owner is at the queue cap, when every owner of the target queue is at the cap, and when the case is closed or under a legal hold. The legacy names the messages and the values to display (the owner, every owner, the target state and the hold state) but no source gives the answer element: whether the refusal carries the owner list and the open-case counts, what the hold answer names, and where the cap and hold state are read from before the operation commits. The cap is a queue column and the hold a case column, so the answer is composed and not stored.
evidence: Legacy section 14 MSG-P3-002 '{owner} is at the caseload cap. Choose another owner or the team queue.' and MSG-P3-005 'This case cannot move to {state} from {current}.'; AC12 'naming every owner of "LIT-BKK-01"'; TSD API-P3-006 lists errors 409 and 422 only, with no response element per error; TSD T3.1 gives queue.capacity_cap (DF-WRK-007), queue_member.capacity (DF-WRK-048) and recovery_case.legal_hold (DF-CAS-020) as columns with no read operation for a pre-check.
area: transfer refusal contract and read model
owner_role: Solution architect, P3; tech lead of rwb-case
proposed: Fix a refusal element with a reason code, the owner list with an open-case count and a cap each, and the current and target state, and state that the cap and the hold are read inside the operation before the first write so a refusal never leaves a partial change.

title: Who may add or retire a transfer reason code is not specified
source: Legacy story RWB E2 012 v2 section 3 (LOV-TRANSFER-REASON, 'new, see Additions') and section 13; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 LOV table; FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.40.3.1
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria (AC3); 11 Data; 13 Solution plan
description: The screen must show the transfer reason codes in force and the operation must refuse a code that is not in them, so the list is reference data read at run time and loaded through the reference-load surface of rwb-case. No source names who may add, change or retire a code: not the role that prepares a load, not the role that approves it, and not whether a change to this list needs the same four-eyes rule as the permission matrix. The six codes the legacy story records are themselves marked 'assumed values', so the set is data with an unstated owner rather than a fixed list.
evidence: Legacy section 3 'LOV-TRANSFER-REASON (new, see Additions) is loaded with the agreed reason codes. Assumed values: R01 Capacity, R02 Customer deceased, R03 Skill, R04 Owner absent, R05 Legal referral, R06 Wrong queue (DL23)'; TSD LOV table 'LOV-TRANSFER-REASON | R01, R02, R03, R04, R05, R06' with no owner column; FSD P3 A2.40.3.1 gives VR-P3-040-1 and VR-P3-040-2 for the refusal and no role for the list; no row of the FSD, the TSD or the two BRDs names a role that may add or retire a code.
proposed: Name the role that may add or retire a transfer reason code and state that a change is a dated reference load approved by a second person, so the list is governed like the permission matrix instead of being edited in place.

title: The activity timeouts and the alert thresholds of the manual move are not specified
source: Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 14 (retry policy only); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41 to 44; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T7 (NFR-008 only)
section: 12 Contract (12.5); 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: The retry policy of the transfer decision is fixed (1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts, NoPackageInForce non-retryable) and the user-facing budget is fixed at 2 s, but no source gives the start-to-close and schedule-to-close values of EvaluateRules and RecordAndApply, nor the values at which an operator should be paged for the move rate, the refusal rate by code, the at-cap hits, the budget breaches and the dead-letter depth. The deployment has to carry values for all of them.
evidence: Temporal and Drools slide 14 'Retry policy: 1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts; NoPackageInForce is non-retryable' — no timeout value; TSD P3 T7 NFR-008 'A screen responds within its target under normal load. Under 2 seconds'; Architecture v5 slide 44 gives the job map and no alert value; no source carries an alert threshold for a transfer path.
legacy_ref: RWB-E2-012 sections 12 and 13 (no timeout or metric value)
owner_role: DevOps lead; service owner of rwb-case
proposed: Confirm the two activity timeouts and the five alert thresholds with the service owner before the capability is switched on in UAT, and record them in the values files as confirmed values rather than defaults.
